title: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali
author: Charles Johnston (trans)
description: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man, an interpretation by Charles Johnston (1867-1931), the Irish Theosophist and Sanskritist (1912). The Yoga Sutras, compiled by Patanjali in the early centuries CE, are the foundational text of classical Raja Yoga: 196 aphorisms in four books defining yoga as the stilling of the fluctuations of consciousness (chitta vritti nirodha). Book I explains concentration and the states of samadhi; Book II the means of practice, the kleshas and the eightfold path of restraints, observances, posture, breath, withdrawal, concentration, meditation and absorption; Book III the powers (siddhis) arising from samyama; and Book IV liberation as the isolation (kaivalya) of pure seeing. Johnston's version offers translation with commentary interpreting the sutras in terms of the 'spiritual man' emerging from the 'psychic man', reflecting Theosophical and Christian mystical sympathies.
